meta.purpose: Age-spread corpus for scoring v2 measurement. Each memory carries created_at_offset_secs; the Rust harness backdates Memory.created_at / accessed_at by that amount before remember so the recency clock has something to decay. SUPERSEDED_FACT_PAIRS guarantee each 'what's the current X' query has a single unambiguous correct answer.

memories.label: sup:release:current
memories.content: Current mnemo release is v0.7.0 — the import name is now mnemo_engine (NAME-1 shipped the rename). Recall scoring v2 also landed here.

memories.label: sup:release:past
memories.content: Current mnemo release is v0.6.1 — the import name is mnemo. BP.1 added mnemo index --rebuild and db.rebuild_index().

memories.label: sup:ann_default:current
memories.content: The default ANN index now uses pq_subspaces = dims / 4 (96 for the 384-d MiniLM embedder). Recall@10 is ~0.98 at 100K memories after this change.

memories.label: sup:ann_default:past
memories.content: The default ANN index uses pq_subspaces = dims / 8 (48 for 384-d vectors), giving ~0.40 recall@10 at 100K memories.

memories.label: sup:lib_name:current
memories.content: The Rust library name is mnemo_engine (Cargo's default from the mnemo-engine package name). CLI binary is still mnemo.

memories.label: sup:lib_name:past
memories.content: The Rust library name is mnemo (set via [lib] name override in Cargo.toml), even though the crate itself is mnemo-engine.

memories.label: sup:fsyncs:current
memories.content: A steady-state flush now costs 3 fsyncs — the pre-flush leased-header write is gone after DUR-1.

memories.label: sup:fsyncs:past
memories.content: A steady-state flush costs 4 fsyncs — data pages, WAL commit, checkpoint, and the pre-flush leased-header write.

memories.label: sup:compact_cache:current
memories.content: mnemo compact preserves the result cache — FIX-1 fixed the pre-v0.6.0 behaviour where compaction silently emptied it.

memories.label: sup:compact_cache:past
memories.content: mnemo compact rewrites the file but empties the result cache; cached values are recomputed on next use.

memories.label: fresh:planner_dispatch
memories.content: Planner dispatched scoring v2: Python only embeds, Rust runs everything else, V1–V5 behind a hidden selector, ship only the winner, query-time only (no format bump).

memories.label: fresh:option_a_rationale
memories.content: Option A chosen for NAME-1: drop the import mnemo alias so the wheel ships no top-level mnemo/ package, ending the collision with mnemo-db and PyPI mnemo in one release instead of two.

memories.label: recent:bp1
memories.content: BP.1 added CLI mnemo index --rebuild and Python db.rebuild_index(); both call Mnemo::rebuild_index on the core which re-runs build_index_with(IndexConfig::default()).

memories.label: recent:dur1
memories.content: DUR-1 landed Option B: a validate_seal failure is always HeaderTampered and never auto-healed; recovery heals only on parse errors (BadMagic, UnsupportedVersion, HeaderChecksum).

memories.label: recent:fix1
memories.content: FIX-1 landed the correctness sweep: compact preserves the cache, export_encrypted refuses live-file overwrite, kdf_params accessor, EmbedCmd rejects zero/non-finite, lazy agent set.

memories.label: recent:py1
memories.content: PY-1 made db.close() release the OS file lock synchronously + released the GIL on flush, recall, verify, rekey, build_index.

memories.label: recent:ann_measured_numbers
memories.content: Measured on M1 Pro, hardware AES, v0.6.1: indexed recall at ~1.4ms / ~9.4ms / ~134ms for 10K / 100K / 1M memories.

memories.label: recent:write_bench
memories.content: Steady-state write benches on v0.6.1: 18.9 ms per single flush, 24.7 ms per batch-of-100 flush — about -13%/-11% vs v0.5.1 after DUR-1 removed one fsync per commit.

memories.label: mid:name1_rename
memories.content: NAME-1 renamed the lib and Python import from mnemo to mnemo_engine to end the collision with mnemo-db.

memories.label: mid:wal_semantics
memories.content: The WAL is a single-fsync commit: data pages copy-on-write, control plane logged, one fsync makes the transaction durable, then a checkpoint folds frames into their home pages.

memories.label: mid:ann_arch
memories.content: ANN index is IVF + Product Quantization: k-means over the vectors gives n_partitions centroids; each partition's vectors are PQ-coded for a compact second-level index.

memories.label: mid:crypto_layers
memories.content: Two-tier key hierarchy: Argon2id derives a KEK from the passphrase; AES-GCM wraps the random DEK with the KEK; the DEK encrypts every page under per-session random nonces.

memories.label: mid:session_api
memories.content: The Session API records conversation turns as working memory; on close it consolidates turns into episodic memory via the normal remember path.

memories.label: mid:mcp_server
memories.content: mnemo serve --mcp runs the MCP JSON-RPC server over stdio; clients can register tools for remember, recall, cache_get, cache_put, compact.

memories.label: old:v0_1_0
memories.content: v0.1.0 was the initial public release of mnemo: four memory types, multi-signal recall, Python bindings, CLI.

memories.label: old:sqlite_analogy
memories.content: Mnemo takes the SQLite position for agent memory: one file, no server, no daemon, no schema migration.

memories.label: old:phase6_methodology
memories.content: Phase 6 benchmarks measure cold recall, warm recall, flush latency, and ANN recall@10 against an exact-scan baseline.

memories.label: old:legacy_scoring
memories.content: The pre-scoring-v2 formula weighted similarity + recency + importance + ln(uses+1), with recency measured from accessed_at so recalls themselves bumped the recency score.

memories.label: old:why_encryption
memories.content: An agent's memory is a valuable, private asset — a long list of past tool outputs, personal preferences, facts. Encrypting at rest makes copying and backup safe by default.

memories.label: old:argon2id_params
memories.content: Default Argon2id params: 19 MiB memory cost, 2 iterations, 1 lane. Takes ~50–100 ms to derive the KEK, which is the point: brute-forcing the passphrase stays expensive.
